purpose: test the hypothesis 'pose is similar, direction differs' for REACHING vs RELEASING
method: for reaching vs releasing, whether locally similar pose states carry OPPOSITE velocity directions
method: standardise the 10-D pose; for each reaching frame, find its k nearest releasing frames (k=50) and compare the sign agreement of the per-channel velocity between the frame and each neighbour
the same comparison within reaching and within releasing gives the reference sign-agreement rate
the statistic that matters is whether CROSS-phase sign agreement is LOWER than WITHIN-phase sign agreement at matched pose locality

matched_neighbour_sign_agreement.definition: fraction of (anchor channel, neighbour channel) pairs whose VELOCITY SIGN agrees, among the k nearest neighbours in standardised shared10 pose space
matched_neighbour_sign_agreement.interpretation_rule: if CROSS-phase sign agreement at matched pose locality is markedly BELOW within-phase agreement, then two phases can occupy similar poses with opposite motion - the premise of the OBS-B hypothesis
